answer: A stake-weighted reputation ledger resists Sybils by making identity expensive: each agent locks a deposit that grows toward its zenith as it earns trust, so spawning many fake identities means locking capital many times over. Honest work builds a durable marble-like record - verifiable, hard to fake, slow to accumulate - while a Sybil's many shallow echoes of activity never reach the same depth. Fraud is punished by slashing the deposit, so faking influence costs real funds.
